falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Fit a Mondrian conformal predictor with reactivity-stratified taxonomy (e.g., low/medium/high resting HRV reactivity quantiles) and compare per-stratum coverage to the original unstratified model using a held-out subject-wise test set. If coverage for high-reactivity subjects reaches the nominal level (e.g., 90%) without degrading other strata, the hypothesis that unmodeled reactivity causes miscalibration is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage for high-reactivity subjects remains significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after adding reactivity strata and controlling for baseline HRV, medication, and circadian phase.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Per-subject resting HRV/EDA baselines, medication logs, recording start times, nonconformity scores per window, and subject-wise train/calibration/test splits preserving independence.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Residual confounding by unmeasured fitness or medication effects could make reactivity strata appear effective when the true cause is another correlated factor.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient calibration samples within high-reactivity strata may yield noisy coverage estimates, masking a real improvement.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Detrend or quality-weight the EDA channel per trial using electrode impedance or SNR proxies, then recompute nonconformity scores and coverage for early vs. late trials. If late-trial undercoverage disappears after correction, sensor drift is falsified as the primary cause.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Late-trial coverage remains significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after applying drift correction and controlling for ambient temperature, humidity, and movement artifacts.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Trial-wise EDA signal quality metrics (impedance or SNR), environmental logs (temperature/humidity), nonconformity scores per trial with order preserved, and subject-wise splits.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Correction may inadvertently remove genuine habituation effects (H9), attributing coverage gain to drift removal when habituation is the true driver.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Impedance/SNR proxies may be too noisy to capture gradual drift, leaving residual drift uncorrected and falsely suggesting drift is not the cause.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Implement a block-conformal or time-aware Mondrian taxonomy that groups windows by transition phase (e.g., stress onset, peak, recovery) and evaluates coverage within each block. If transitional-block coverage reaches nominal levels while stationary blocks remain calibrated, the exchangeability violation hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage in transitional blocks stays significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after adding transition-phase strata and controlling for respiration, posture, and substance use.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Window-level HRV features with temporal order, respiration rate/depth, posture labels, pre-study substance use, nonconformity residuals per window, and subject-wise splits.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Improved coverage could stem from increased stratum sample sizes rather than restored exchangeability, conflating small-stratum effects (H8) with non-stationarity.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Block definition may be too coarse, leaving residual temporal dependence within blocks and failing to detect the violation.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Identify potentially mislabeled trials using objective stress markers (e.g., cortisol) or self-report consistency metrics, then reassign stratum labels for those trials and recompute coverage. If coverage normalizes for previously undercovered strata after correction, mislabeling is falsified as the main driver.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Stratum-specific coverage remains significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after relabeling trials flagged by objective markers and controlling for personality, fatigue, and scale interpretation.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Per-subject self-report reliability scores, personality questionnaire data, trial-wise cortisol or other objective stress markers, nonconformity distributions per stratum, and subject-wise splits.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Objective markers may be sparse or noisy, leading to incorrect relabeling that artificially improves coverage without addressing the true mechanism.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Mislabeling may be systematic but subtle, escaping detection by available consistency checks, so coverage stays low despite correction attempts.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Augment the Mondrian taxonomy with age decile strata (or age-aware covariate-adjusted nonconformity) and evaluate per-age-group coverage on a held-out set. If older-age coverage reaches nominal levels without harming younger groups, the demographic underrepresentation hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage for age >50 (or highest decile) remains significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after adding age strata and controlling for comorbidities, medication load, and fitness.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Demographic and clinical metadata (age, comorbidities, medications), baseline HRV/EDA per subject, fitness proxy, nonconformity scores per stratum, and subject-wise splits preserving age distribution.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Age strata may capture fitness or medication effects rather than age per se, attributing coverage gain to age stratification when the true confounder is fitness.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Older subjects may be too few to form stable strata, yielding high-variance coverage estimates that obscure a real effect.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Compute nonconformity scores using multiple candidate functions (softmax margin, Mahalanobis distance, conformalized quantile regression) on standardized multimodal features with missing-modality indicators, then compare per-stratum coverage. If an alternative score yields nominal coverage across all strata while the original margin score does not, the score-misalignment hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: All candidate nonconformity scores show significantly below-nominal coverage (e.g., <85% at 90% target) for the same strata after controlling for feature scaling, missing modalities, and classifier architecture.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Standardized multimodal features per window, modality-presence indicators, nonconformity scores for each candidate function, per-stratum coverage results, and subject-wise splits.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: An alternative score may appear better due to overfitting to the calibration set, not because it aligns with true feature geometry.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: The set of candidate scores may not include the truly appropriate geometry-aware function, leading to a false conclusion that score choice is not the issue.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Create day-specific Mondrian strata (or apply batch-effect correction such as ComBat on features) and evaluate coverage per day on a day-wise holdout. If day-level coverage reaches nominal levels and day-to-day variance in nonconformity quantiles disappears, the batch-effect hypothesis is falsified.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage for at least one recording day remains significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after day-aware stratification or batch correction, controlling for experimenter, equipment changes, and sleep quality.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Day identifier, ambient temperature/humidity logs, experimenter IDs, pre-session sleep diaries or actigraphy, nonconformity scores grouped by day, and splits respecting day boundaries.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Day stratification may inadvertently capture habituation across days (H9), attributing coverage improvement to batch correction when habituation is the true cause.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Batch effects may be non-linear or interact with subject-specific factors, so simple day strata or linear correction fail to remove the shift, leaving undercoverage.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Add trial-index as a stratification variable (early vs. middle vs. late trials) in the Mondrian taxonomy and compare coverage per trial block. If late-trial coverage reaches nominal levels while early-trial coverage stays calibrated, habituation is falsified as the sole cause of undercoverage.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Late-trial coverage remains significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after trial-aware stratification and controlling for fatigue ratings, inter-trial interval, and time-of-day.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Trial index, inter-trial intervals, subjective fatigue ratings per trial, time-of-day per trial, trial-wise physiological feature trajectories, nonconformity scores per trial, and subject-wise splits.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Trial stratification may also capture sensor drift (H2) or day effects (H7), conflating habituation with those mechanisms.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Habituation may be non-monotonic or subject-specific, so coarse trial blocks fail to model the trajectory, leaving residual undercoverage.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Incorporate missingness indicators for each modality (especially respiration) as explicit features in the nonconformity score, and compare coverage for windows with vs. without missing respiration. If coverage for missing-respiration windows reaches nominal levels while complete-case coverage is unchanged, informative missingness is falsified as the primary driver.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage for windows with missing respiration remains significantly below nominal (e.g., <85% at 90% target) after adding missingness indicators and controlling for movement intensity, imputation method, and multi-modality dropout.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Per-window missingness logs per modality, accelerometer-derived movement intensity, imputation method used, nonconformity scores for complete-case, imputed, and missingness-aware models, and subject-wise splits.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Missingness indicators may correlate with stress level itself, so improved coverage could reflect better stress discrimination rather than correction of informative missingness.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: If missingness is perfectly collinear with high movement (which also degrades other modalities), the indicator adds no new information and the test cannot isolate the missingness effect.
